verses.1: And the LORD answered Job out of the storm, saying:
verses.2: "Will the one who disputes with the Almighty teach him? Let God answer him, if he will.
verses.3: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
verses.4: "Behold, I am of little account; what shall I answer you? I lay my hand over my mouth.
verses.5: Once I have spoken, and I will not answer; twice, and I will say no more.
verses.6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm, saying:
verses.7: "Now gird yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall make me know.
verses.8: "Will you disannul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
verses.9: "Do you have an arm like God? Or a voice like him thundering?
verses.10: "Now gird yourself with glory and majesty, clothe yourself with splendor and beauty.
verses.11: "Pour out the rage of your anger, and look on every proud one, and humble him;
verses.12: "Look on every proud one, bring him low, and subdue the wicked where they stand.
verses.13: "Hide them all in the dust together, their faces with the dust of the pit.
verses.14: "And I will myself commend you, for you will save me with your right hand.
verses.15: "Behold now, the beasts I have made with you; they eat grass like the ox.
verses.16: "Behold now, their strength is in their loins, and their might is in the muscles of their belly.
verses.17: "Their tail sways like a cedar, the sinews of their thighs are interwoven.
verses.18: "Their bones are rods of bronze, their limbs like bars of iron.
verses.19: "He is the first of the works of God; let the one who made him draw near to him with his sword.
verses.20: "For the mountains bring him their produce, and all the beasts of the field play there.
verses.21: "He lies beneath the lotus trees, in the covert of the reeds and marsh.
verses.22: "The shade of the lotus trees covers him, and the willows of the stream surround him.
verses.23: "When the river overflows, it does not alarm him; he trusts, though the Jordan rushes to his mouth.
verses.24: "In his eyes he takes them in, arrows pierce his eye.
verses.25: "He draws the leviathan with a hook, and with a rope he binds the tongue of the serpent.
verses.26: "Will you put a crest in his nose, and pierce his jaw with a hook?
verses.27: "Will he make many pleas to you? Will he speak to you gentle words?
verses.28: "Will he make a covenant with you? Will he take him as a servant forever?
verses.29: "Will you play with him as with a bird, or bind him for your handmaidens?
verses.30: "Will companions trade him for pieces, will they divide him among the merchants?
verses.31: "Will you fill his hide with scales, and his head with the shadow of the sea?
verses.32: "Put your hand on him; remember the battle—do not repeat it anymore."

notes:
Notes
- v. 19: "He is the first of the works of God" — the Hebrew uses מִשְׁנֶה (mishneh), which may also be rendered "offspring" or "duplicate," but "first" is chosen here for clarity and the context of divine creation.
